title: Automated Logistics Manifest Digitization
business: A regional freight logistics company managing thousands of handwritten and printed shipping manifests daily.
problem: Manual data entry from paper-based shipping manifests is prone to human error, creates significant processing delays, and prevents real-time inventory tracking.
solution: Amazon Textract automates the extraction of printed text, handwriting, tables, and forms from scanned manifests, converting unstructured paper documents into machine-readable JSON data for downstream logistics systems.
steps: Upload scanned manifest images to an Amazon S3 bucket.
Trigger an AWS Lambda function upon S3 object creation.
Call the AnalyzeDocument API to extract tables and key-value pairs.
Parse the returned JSON response to map fields like 'Tracking Number' and 'Weight' to the database.
Update the logistics management system with the extracted data.
outcome: The company achieves rapid, accurate data ingestion from physical documents, enabling immediate visibility into shipment status without manual intervention.
limitation: Textract may struggle with low-resolution scans or highly distorted handwriting, which can lead to extraction errors; developers should implement a confidence score threshold check to flag low-confidence results for human review.
